HEREDITARY CANCER SYNDROME GENETIC TESTING REPORT

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Provider: [redacted name], MD
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
This 45-year-old patient was referred for hereditary cancer genetic testing due to a personal history of colorectal cancer diagnosed at age 43. Family history is significant for colorectal cancer in the father at age 50 and endometrial cancer in the paternal grandmother at age 52, raising suspicion for Lynch syndrome.

TEST PERFORMED
Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) Hereditary Cancer Panel
- Analysis of 77 genes associated with hereditary cancer syndromes
- Full gene sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis
- Minimum coverage: 50x; Average coverage: 250x
- Platform: Illumina NextSeq 550
- Bioinformatics pipeline version 3.2

GENES ANALYZED
APC, ATM, AXIN2, BAP1, BARD1, BMPR1A, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CDH1, CDK4, CDKN2A, CHEK2, DICER1, EPCAM, FH, FLCN, GREM1, HOXB13, KIT, MAX, MEN1, MET, MITF, MLH1, MLH3, MSH2, MSH3, MSH6, MUTYH, NBN, NF1, NF2, NTHL1, PALB2, PDGFRA, PMS2, POLD1, POLE, POT1, PRKAR1A, PTCH1, PTEN, RAD50, RAD51C, RAD51D, RB1, RECQL4, RET, RUNX1, SDHA, SDHAF2, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SMAD4, SMARCA4, SMARCB1, SMARCE1, STK11, SUFU, TMEM127, TP53, TSC1, TSC2, VHL, WRN, WT1, XRCC2

RESULTS

PATHOGENIC VARIANT DETECTED:

MLH1 (NM_000249.3): c.350C>T p.(Thr117Met)
- Zygosity: Heterozygous
- Classification: Pathogenic (Class 5)
- VAF (Variant Allele Frequency): 48%
- Coverage at position: 312x

This missense variant results in substitution of threonine with methionine at codon 117, affecting a highly conserved residue within the ATPase domain of the MLH1 protein. This variant has been reported in multiple Lynch syndrome families and segregates with disease. Functional studies demonstrate impaired mismatch repair activity.

SUPPORTING TUMOR STUDIES:
- Immunohistochemistry (IHC): Loss of MLH1 protein expression
- Microsatellite Instability (MSI): High (MSI-H)
- These findings are consistent with MLH1 deficiency

OTHER FINDINGS:
No additional pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in the remaining 76 genes analyzed.

INTERPRETATION
The identification of a pathogenic MLH1 variant confirms the diagnosis of Lynch syndrome (hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer, HNPCC). This autosomal dominant condition is associated with significantly increased lifetime cancer risks:

- Colorectal cancer: 52-82% lifetime risk
- Endometrial cancer (females): 25-60% lifetime risk
- Gastric cancer: 6-13% lifetime risk
- Ovarian cancer (females): 4-12% lifetime risk
- Small bowel, urinary tract, brain, and sebaceous neoplasms: increased risk

The patient's personal history of colorectal cancer at age 43 and family history of Lynch-associated cancers are consistent with this diagnosis.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. COLORECTAL CANCER SURVEILLANCE:
   - Colonoscopy every 1-2 years beginning immediately
   - Consider aspirin chemoprevention (discuss with oncologist)

2. GYNECOLOGIC CANCER RISK REDUCTION (if applicable):
   - Annual endometrial sampling beginning at age 30-35
   - Transvaginal ultrasound can be considered but has limited sensitivity
   - Discuss prophylactic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy after completion of childbearing

3. OTHER CANCER SURVEILLANCE:
   - Upper endoscopy with visualization of the duodenum every 3-5 years beginning at age 30-35
   - Annual urinalysis beginning at age 30-35
   - Consider annual physical and neurological examination
   - Consideration of pancreatic cancer screening in families with pancreatic cancer history

4. FAMILY TESTING:
   - Cascade genetic testing is strongly recommended for all first-degree relatives
   - Testing can be performed as early as age 18 (or earlier if clinically indicated)
   - At-risk relatives who test negative for the familial variant can follow general population screening guidelines

5. GENETIC COUNSELING:
   - Recommend genetic counseling for the patient and at-risk family members
   - Discussion of reproductive options including preimplantation genetic testing

6. CLINICAL MANAGEMENT:
   - Coordinate care with high-risk cancer genetics clinic
   - Regular review of surveillance recommendations as guidelines evolve

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted laboratory name]. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Laboratory Director
[redacted date]
